title: Alma Teaches Privately
summary: Alma privately teaches willing listeners the words of Abinadi, including teachings about Christ, resurrection, redemption, and ascension; many believe.

explicit_facts.text: Alma repented and went about privately among the people, teaching Abinadi's words.
The teachings concerned what was to come, resurrection, redemption through Christ's power, sufferings, death, resurrection, and ascension.
Alma taught those who would hear, privately so the king would not learn of it, and many believed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma speaks quietly to a small group of listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact location, time of day, and appearance of Alma and the listeners.

narration.text: And many did believe his words.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The cited teachings are described in narration, not given as verbatim dialogue from Alma.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ or the resurrection as a visible event.

title: The Believers Go to Mormon
summary: Believers go to Mormon, where Alma hides by a fountain near a thicket during the day; they come there to hear him.

explicit_facts.text: Those who believed went to a place called Mormon.
Mormon had a fountain of pure water and a nearby thicket of small trees; Alma hid there by day from the king's searches.
Believers went there to hear Alma's words.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A fountain and a thicket of small trees are near one another.
unspecified_visual_details: The landscape beyond the fountain and thicket, and the appearance of the people.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict wild beasts; the text says the borders were infested by them at times, but does not describe an encounter.

title: A Gathering at Mormon
summary: After many days, a goodly number of believers gather at Mormon to hear Alma teach repentance, redemption, and faith on the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: After many days, a goodly number of believers gathered at Mormon to hear Alma.
Alma taught and preached repentance, redemption, and faith on the Lord.

unspecified_visual_details: The number of people, their arrangement, and the exact setting within Mormon.

title: Alma Invites Them to Covenant
summary: Alma asks whether the gathered people desire to enter God's fold and make a covenant through baptism, serving God and keeping his commandments.

explicit_facts.text: Alma calls the water the waters of Mormon and asks whether they desire to come into God's fold and be called his people.
He describes willingness to bear one another's burdens, mourn with those who mourn, comfort those needing comfort, and witness of God until death.
Alma asks whether they are willing to be baptized in the name of the Lord as a witness of a covenant to serve him and keep his commandments.

unspecified_visual_details: The listeners' specific reactions during the address.

title: The People's Answer

explicit_facts.text: The Spirit of the Lord was upon Alma, and Alma baptized Helam by authority from God, speaking of their covenant and the Spirit.

title: The Baptisms at Mormon
summary: Alma baptizes those who come to Mormon, about two hundred and four people; they are filled with God's grace and called the church of God, or the church of Christ.

explicit_facts.text: Alma baptized those who came to Mormon, about two hundred and four souls, in the waters of Mormon.

title: Alma Ordains Priests

explicit_facts.text: Alma, having authority from God, ordained priests at a ratio of one priest for every fifty people.

title: Instructions for Teaching
summary: Alma commands the priests to teach the prophets' teachings and preach repentance and faith on the Lord, without contention, in unity and love.

explicit_facts.text: Alma commanded the priests to teach only what he had taught and what the holy prophets had spoken.
He commanded them to preach only repentance and faith on the Lord, who had redeemed his people.
He commanded them to avoid contention and to be united in faith and love.
Alma commanded them to preach in this manner; they became the children of God.

title: Further Instructions to the Priests
summary: Alma commands Sabbath observance, daily thanksgiving, priestly labor for support, and regular gatherings to teach and worship.

explicit_facts.text: Alma commanded the people to observe the Sabbath and give thanks to the Lord every day.
He commanded the priests to labor with their hands for their support rather than depend on the people.
One day each week was set apart for gathering to teach and worship; they were also to assemble as often as they could.
The priests were to receive God's grace through their labor, grow strong in the Spirit, gain knowledge of God, and teach with power and authority from God.

title: Sharing with Those in Need
summary: Alma commands the people to share according to their means, give to those in need, and impart to one another according to need and want.

explicit_facts.text: Alma commanded church members to share their substance according to what each had.
Those with more should give more; those with little were required to give little, and those without should be given to.
They should give freely to priests in need and to every needy, naked soul.
They imparted to one another temporally and spiritually according to needs and wants.
